label: FP
reason: The XSS alert references user-provided values flowing into HTML output via cookie name and value concatenation, but these values originate from request parameters that are filtered out early in the logic (only used to set param and then ignored), and the actual output uses a generated random key which is not derived from user input. The user-provided value is only used to set a variable name and is not directly injected into the response body. Furthermore, the random number generation occurs independently and is properly sanitized via substring operation on a non-user-controlled value. There is no path where untrusted user input reaches the sink.

evidence.note: param is only used to set a variable name and is not passed to output; random value generated and used exclusively
